title: Homogeneous line bundles have coroot degree on simple Schubert curves
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $G$ be a semisimple simply connected $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme]: smooth, connected, affine and of finite type, with no nontrivial smooth connected solvable normal subgroup, and such that every surjective homomorphism from a semisimple group with finite central kernel is an isomorphism. Solvable means that successive commutator subgroup schemes become trivial; central means commuting after every scalar extension. Fix a split maximal torus $T\subseteq B\subseteq G$, where $B$ is a Borel subgroup. Use the character lattice $X^*(T)$, positive roots in $\operatorname{Lie}(B)$, simple roots $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_r$, their coroots, and $p:B\to T$ of [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. Write $Q=G/B$ and $W=N_G(T)(F)/T(F)$, choose representatives $n_w$, and use $w_0$ and the open cell $C=Un_{w_0}B/B$ of [lem-sfb-bruhat-longest-cell-charts], where $U$ is the unipotent radical of $B$. Set $s_j=s_{\alpha_j}\in W$, the reflection of [lem-sfb-reductive-rank-one-reflections] acting by $s_{\alpha_j}(x)=x-\langle x,\alpha_j^\vee\rangle\alpha_j$, and $R_j=\overline{Bn_{s_j}B/B}_{\mathrm{red}}\subseteq Q$. For any character $\lambda\in X^*(T)$ put $M_\lambda=\mathcal L_{-\lambda\circ p}$ [lem-sfb-homogeneous-line-bundle-sections], with quotient action $(g,z)\cdot b=(gb,\lambda(p(b))z)$. Let $B_2\subseteq\operatorname{SL}_{2,F}$ be the upper triangular subgroup. There is a homomorphism $v_j:\operatorname{SL}_{2,F}\to G$ whose restriction to $\operatorname{diag}(t,t^{-1})$ is $\alpha_j^\vee(t)$, with $v_j(B_2)\subseteq B$, inducing an isomorphism $$\overline v_j:\operatorname{SL}_{2,F}/B_2\xrightarrow{\sim}R_j.$$ Identify $\operatorname{SL}_{2,F}/B_2$ with $\mathbf P^1_F$ by sending $gB_2$ to the line spanned by its first column. For $m=\langle\lambda,\alpha_j^\vee\rangle$ one has $$\overline v_j^*(M_\lambda|_{R_j})\simeq\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^1_F}(m),\qquad \deg(M_\lambda|_{R_j})=\langle\lambda,\alpha_j^\vee\rangle,$$ where the twists are tensor powers of the dual tautological line for $m\geq0$ and their duals for $m<0$, and degree means [def-pc-degree-line-bundle]. No dominance or characteristic hypothesis is imposed on $\lambda$. For $r=0$ there are no assertions indexed by $j$.

source.place: Section 2.1, the minimal parabolics P_i and Schubert curves X_(s_i), printed pp.62--63, equation (7); the degree computation underlying Exercise 2.2.E(3), printed p.71. Rank-one subgroup construction: Milne iAG2017, Theorem 21.11(b),(e), printed pp.429--430, and paragraph 21.24, printed p.432 (using 20.32). The statement records the rank-one restriction computation separately from the Picard basis. Local PDF WANTED; primary author-hosted PDF read online.

proof.text: Fix an index $j$, put $\alpha=\alpha_j$, and take $I=\{\alpha\}$ in [lem-sfb-standard-parabolic-levi-charts]. Write $H=L_I$, $B_H=B\cap H$, $P=P_I$ and $R=R_I$. This gives the root system $\{\alpha,-\alpha\}$ in $H$, positive root $\alpha$ in $B_H$, and $P=R\rtimes H$, $B=R\rtimes B_H$. The rank-one construction [lem-sfb-reductive-rank-one-reflections] gives $v:\operatorname{SL}_2\to H\subseteq G$ with central kernel, image $D=H^{\mathrm{der}}$, upper root subgroup isomorphic to $U_\alpha$, and $v(\operatorname{diag}(a,a^{-1}))=\alpha^\vee(a)$. Every upper triangular determinant-one matrix is a product of a diagonal matrix and an upper unitriangular matrix. Both factors map into $B_H$, so $v(B_2)\subseteq B$.

The matrix models of [lem-sfb-split-rank-one-classification] identify $(H,T)$ with a torus times $\operatorname{SL}_2$, $\operatorname{PGL}_2$ or $\operatorname{GL}_2$, and identify $D$ with the corresponding special/projective special linear factor. Choose the upper orientation to be $\alpha$. In these coordinates $B_H$ is the upper triangular subgroup: apply [lem-sfb-regular-cocharacter-borel-description] to $H$; for a regular cocharacter positive on $\alpha$, the matrix limit condition says precisely that the lower-left entry vanishes. Put $B_D=D\cap B_H$. The map $D/B_D\to H/B_H$ is an isomorphism of fppf coset sheaves. Indeed torus factors lie in $B_H$; in the $\operatorname{GL}_2$ case an invertible matrix $g$ is $[g\operatorname{diag}(\det(g)^{-1},1)]\operatorname{diag}(\det(g),1)$, with the first factor in $\operatorname{SL}_2$ and the second upper triangular; equality of two cosets is exactly that their ratio lies in $D\cap B_H$. These formulas also give the inverse locally in the projective matrix quotient.

source.place: 20.33, pp.419; 21.29--21.32, pp.433--435; elementary matrix calculation of the rank-one quotient.

proof.text: The central kernel $K$ of $v$ is contained in $\mu_2\subseteq\operatorname{SL}_2$: commuting with the universal matrices $I+xE_{12}$ and $I+yE_{21}$ forces a central matrix to be scalar, and determinant one forces its scalar square to be one. This works over every algebra, including characteristic two. Thus $K$ is finite and diagonalizable by [lem-sfb-split-torus-subgroups-diagonalizable]. The image-factorization theorem [lem-sfb-affine-homomorphism-flat-image] makes $v:\operatorname{SL}_2\to D$ faithfully flat (its image is $D$ by Step 1). Apply [lem-sfb-central-isogeny-borel-root-compatibility] to this map and the pair in $D$. The preimage $v^{-1}(B_D)$ is a Borel containing $B_2$, hence equals $B_2$. Here $B_2$ is indeed a Borel: the regular cocharacter $a\mapsto\operatorname{diag}(a,a^{-1})$ has limit subgroup exactly the upper triangular matrices, by [lem-sfb-regular-cocharacter-borel-description]. The quotient isomorphism of [lem-sfb-multiplicative-isogeny-borel-comparison] now gives $\operatorname{SL}_2/B_2\simeq D/B_D\simeq H/B_H$, induced by the actual $v$.

The first-column map identifies $\operatorname{SL}_2/B_2$ with $\mathbf P^1_F$. On $U_0$ with coordinates $[1:t]$ and $U_1$ with coordinates $[s:1]$ take the determinant-one lifts $$a_0(t)=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\ t&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad a_1(s)=\begin{pmatrix}s&-1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}.$$ They are regular sections of the first-column map. Two determinant-one matrices with the same first-column line differ on the right by an upper triangular determinant-one matrix, after choosing a local generator of that line. Thus these two sections give mutually inverse maps on the fppf quotient, with overlap $s=t^{-1}$, and identify the quotient as a scheme, not just its field-valued points.

source.place: Example 18.17, p.391; explicit standard-chart verification of the first-column quotient.

proof.text: The semidirect products in [lem-sfb-standard-parabolic-levi-charts] identify $P/B$ with $H/B_H$: send $rhB$ to $hB_H$; multiplying on the right by $r'b$ changes this to $hbB_H$, since $R$ is normal and contained in $B$. Conversely $hB_H\mapsto hB$ is inverse. Quotients and local lifts are scheme-theoretic by [lem-sfb-homogeneous-orbit-quotient-geometry]. The map $P/B\to G/B$ is a monomorphism: locally lift two test-scheme points to $P$; their equal images mean that their ratio lies in $B$, which is precisely equality in $P/B$. The source $H/B_H$ is proper by [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure], and $G/B$ is separated by the same properness clause. Therefore [lemma-nagata-proper-to-separated-target] makes this map proper, and [lem-pc-proper-monomorphism-closed] makes it a closed immersion. Its source is reduced, since by Steps 3--4 it is $\mathbf P^1_F$.

source.place: 21.90--21.91, pp.453--454; quotient construction 18c; closed-image argument using the cited proper-monomorphism criterion.

proof.text: Under $P/B=H/B_H$, the normal subgroup $R\subset B$ acts trivially, so the $B$-orbits are the $B_H$-orbits. In the three matrix models of [lem-sfb-split-rank-one-classification], upper triangular matrices on first-column lines have exactly the fixed line $[1:0]$ and its complement $\{[s:1]\}$, the latter an affine-line orbit. The image of $w=\begin{pmatrix}0&-1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$ is a representative of $s_\alpha$: conjugating the diagonal sends $a$ to $a^{-1}$ and in the rank-one models it normalizes the full diagonal torus $T$, giving the unique nonidentity normalizer class of [lem-sfb-reductive-rank-one-reflections]. Hence its $B$-orbit in $G/B$ is exactly $Bn_{s_j}B/B$; any other chosen representative differs by $T\subset B$. This orbit is dense in the closed reduced image from Step 5, since it is the complement of one point in $\mathbf P^1$. Its reduced closure is therefore precisely that image. This proves $\overline v_j:\operatorname{SL}_2/B_2\simeq R_j$.

source.place: 21.11(d), p.429--430; 21.91, pp.453--454. Brion--Kumar §2.1, pp.62--63, gives the same minimal-parabolic/Schubert-curve identification.

proof.text: Write $m=\langle\lambda,\alpha^\vee\rangle$. By [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure] the pairing means $\lambda(\alpha^\vee(a))=a^m$. On $B_2$, the character $\lambda p v$ is therefore $a^m$ on $\operatorname{diag}(a,a^{-1})$ and is one on the upper unitriangular subgroup, since its image lies in $U_\alpha\subseteq R_u(B)$ by [lem-sfb-borel-root-product-coordinates]. Pulling back the quotient bundle of [lem-sfb-homogeneous-line-bundle-sections] along $\overline v_j$ gives the bundle with quotient relation $(g,z)\sim(gb,a^m z)$ for $b=\begin{pmatrix}a&c\\0&a^{-1}\end{pmatrix}$. Explicitly, its map to the pullback sends $[g,z]$ to $(gB_2,[v(g),z])$. On the two sections $a_i$ of Step 4 it is the identity on the fibre coordinate, hence an isomorphism; this verifies pullback compatibility directly from the quotient relation.

source.place: 18c, pp.389--391; quotient construction and Example 18.17. Explicit pullback of the associated bundle.

proof.text: On the overlap of the two charts, direct multiplication gives $$a_0(t)^{-1}a_1(t^{-1})=\begin{pmatrix}t^{-1}&-1\\0&t\end{pmatrix}.$$ Let $e_i=[a_i,1]$ be the local bundle frame. The quotient action in Step 7 gives $[a_1,t^{-m}]=[a_0,1]$, so $e_0=t^{-m}e_1$. This is exactly the transition of $\mathcal O(m)$ in [def-pc-projective-space-twist]. To check the stated dual-tautological convention, the tautological frames $q_0=(1,t)$ and $q_1=(t^{-1},1)$ satisfy $q_0=tq_1$; their duals satisfy $q_0^*=t^{-1}q_1^*$. Tensor powers and duals give $t^{-m}$ for every integer $m$, proving the required isomorphism with precisely its asserted sign.

source.place: Example 18.17, p.391; explicit overlap calculation, using the cited definition of twists.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-projective-space-twist-cohomology] with $A=F$, $n=1$ and $d=m$. For $m\geq0$ the degree-zero dimension is $m+1$ and all higher cohomology vanishes. For $m=-1$ every group is zero. For $m\leq-2$ the only nonzero group is $H^1$, of dimension $-m-1$ (count the pairs of strictly negative exponents summing to $m$). Thus in all cases $\chi(\mathcal O(m))=m+1$ and $\chi(\mathcal O)=1$. Definition [def-pc-degree-line-bundle] gives $\deg\mathcal O(m)=m$. The isomorphism $\overline v_j$ identifies the sheaves, their sections on every open, and therefore their cohomology and Euler characteristics, so $\deg(M_\lambda|_{R_j})=m$. There was no division by the characteristic or sign restriction on $m$. If $r=0$ there was no index to choose and all indexed assertions are vacuous.
